title: Mongo to Postgres pipeline: clean, load, transform, deliver, read back
proves: a project cleans a MongoDB collection and a PostgreSQL table, writes 12 raw documents to Mongo, reads them back and writes the transformed rows to Postgres, then reads the table back

the transform turns a noisy text amount (thousands commas, decimal point, spaces) into whole cents and a noisy status (case, space) into a lower case status; the test compares each row of the table with its Mongo document (the cents before they became text)

the run checks values: an <assert> on every readback row (status set, amount range) and on a totals row (count, id sum, amount sum, status count); a failed assert stops a normal run (negative run_assert_amount_sum_wrong)
a normal run twice gives the same rows: the clear of both targets runs first
Build reads the raw documents (seed.json) and the table (seed.sql) and proves the products against them; it isolates the writes and skips the clears, so it does not prove the delivery
the tables come from db/seed.sql, which the test runs before Build and the runs, because Build refuses an <execute> step
the literal counts on the source read and the readback work around #493 for the readback step
this project needs the MongoDB and PostgreSQL services: it runs in the external-service test job

negatives.name: run_assert_amount_sum_wrong
negatives.expected: The table does not hold the 12 transformed orders
negatives.run_error: The table does not hold the 12 transformed orders
